stages.title: Greek Alphabet and Reading
stages.summary: The twenty-four letters, the marks written over and under them, and reading Greek words aloud.

units.title: The letters
units.summary: Lower case, capitals and the two shapes of sigma.

units.title: Vowels and marks
units.summary: Vowels, diphthongs, breathings, accents and the other signs of a printed Greek text.

units.title: Reading aloud
units.summary: Syllables, stress and the traditions of pronunciation.

stages.title: Nominal Foundations
stages.summary: The article, the five cases, the first two declensions, adjectives, pronouns, prepositions and the simplest sentences.

units.title: The article and the cases
units.summary: What each case does in a clause, read first from the article.

lessons.title: Nominative and accusative: subject and object

units.title: The first two declensions
units.summary: The endings of the commonest nouns and of the adjectives that follow them.

The vocative, and the five cases together

units.title: Small words and first sentences
units.summary: Pronouns, prepositions and the verb 'to be'.

stages.title: Verbal Foundations
stages.summary: The indicative in all its tenses and voices, with the stems, augment and reduplication that build them.

units.title: Present and imperfect
units.summary: Person and number, the three voices, contraction and the augment.

lessons.title: Middle and passive in the present

units.title: Future and aorist
units.summary: The sigmatic tenses, the second aorist and the aorist passive.

units.title: The perfect and the verb as a whole
units.summary: Reduplication, the six principal parts, and the verbs that go their own way.

lessons.title: Perfect, pluperfect and the principal parts

stages.title: Advanced Nominal Morphology
stages.summary: The third declension, the remaining adjective classes, comparison, the pronouns and the numerals.

units.title: The third declension
units.summary: Consonant stems, vowel stems and the nouns that are irregular.

lessons.title: Third declension: vowel stems and irregular nouns
Adjectives of the third declension: πᾶς, πολύς, μέγας, ἀληθής

units.title: Pronouns and numerals
units.summary: This and that, who and which, who? and someone, self and each other, one to twelve.

lessons.title: τίς and τις: interrogative and indefinite
Adjectives and participles used as nouns

stages.title: Mood, Aspect, and Verbal Syntax
stages.summary: The moods beyond the indicative, the infinitive and participle as forms, and the sentences built with them.

units.title: The moods
units.summary: Subjunctive, imperative and optative.

lessons.title: Purpose and result: ἵνα, ὅπως, ὥστε

units.title: Infinitive and participle: the forms
units.summary: The verbal noun and the verbal adjective, tense by tense.

units.title: Sentences
units.summary: Conditions and reported speech.

stages.title: Participles and Complex Syntax
stages.summary: What participles and infinitives do in a sentence, and how Greek joins clauses into periods.

units.title: Participles at work
units.summary: The participle as adjective, as noun and as adverbial clause.

units.title: Infinitives, clauses and the sentence
units.summary: The infinitive at work, relative clauses, connectives, and parsing a whole period.

stages.title: New Testament Greek Reading
stages.summary: Sustained reading, author by author, from the plainest Greek of the New Testament to the hardest.

units.title: Gospels and Acts
units.summary: John, Mark, Luke and Acts.

units.title: Letters and the Apocalypse
units.summary: Paul, the general epistles, Hebrews and Revelation.

stages.title: Septuagint and Apostolic Fathers
stages.summary: Greek translated from Hebrew, and the Greek of the generation after the apostles.
stages.statusNote: The Apostolic Fathers unit is populated from the library's editions, whose linguistic analysis is automatic and unchecked (lessons say so). The Septuagint unit is defined but awaits an analysed Septuagint: the library holds a Septuagint text for reading, with no lemmas or morphology, so no exercise can be drawn from it.

units.title: The Apostolic Fathers
units.summary: The Didache, First Clement, Ignatius and Polycarp.

units.title: The Septuagint
units.summary: Awaiting an analysed Septuagint.

stages.title: Patristic and Theological Greek
stages.summary: The Greek of the fourth-century theologians and the words on which their arguments turn.
stages.statusNote: Populated from Athanasius, On the Incarnation, the one fourth-century Greek work in the library with a linguistic analysis (automatic and unchecked). Justin, Irenaeus, Basil, the two Gregories, Chrysostom and Cyril await analysed Greek editions.

units.title: Athanasius
units.summary: On the Incarnation, and the theological vocabulary it shares with the New Testament.

lessons.title: Theological vocabulary: λόγος, φύσις, οὐσία, χάρις, πίστις, δικαιοσύνη

stages.title: Advanced Greek Literature
stages.summary: Optional pathways beyond the Koine and the Fathers.
stages.statusNote: Classical, Hellenistic, Byzantine and philosophical Greek, advanced patristic theology and textual criticism are a later expansion. The library holds no analysed text of these varieties, and the course does not claim to teach them. The data model already keeps varieties apart (grc-cla, grc-koi, grc-pat, grc-byz) so that they can be added without changing lexical identities.

objectives.can: Name each of the twenty-four lower-case letters and give its sound.
Match capital letters to their lower-case forms and read σ and ς as one letter.
Tell long vowels from short, recognise the diphthongs, and read a vowel with iota subscript.
Read rough and smooth breathings and name the acute, grave and circumflex accents.
Divide a Greek word into syllables, find its stressed syllable, and read a verse aloud in one consistent pronunciation.
Give the case, number and gender of any form of the article.
Recognise ten of the commonest nouns of the New Testament.
Tell a nominative from an accusative and say which is the subject and which the object of a clause.
Recognise ten more common nouns.
Recognise genitive and dative forms and give the commonest sense of each.
Recognise ten more common nouns.
Parse and form second-declension masculine and neuter nouns.
Recognise ten common second-declension nouns.
Parse and form first-declension nouns, feminine and masculine.
Recognise ten common first-declension nouns.
Recognise a vocative and distinguish all five cases of a first- or second-declension noun.
Match an adjective to its noun in case, number and gender, in attributive and predicate position.
Recognise ten common adjectives.
Parse the forms of ἐγώ, σύ and αὐτός and say whom each refers to.
Say which case a preposition is governing and how the case changes its sense.
Recognise the twelve commonest prepositions.
Parse the present and imperfect indicative of εἰμί.
Read a sentence with εἰμί, finding its subject and predicate, including where the verb is left out.
Give the person and number of a present active indicative and name its subject.
Recognise ten of the commonest verbs.
Recognise the present forms of verbs in -έω, -άω and -όω and name their uncontracted headword.
Recognise present middle and passive forms and tell from the context which voice is meant.
Recognise ten common verbs that are middle in form.
Recognise an imperfect indicative by its augment and endings and parse it.
Recognise and parse future indicative forms, active, middle and passive.
Recognise first-aorist active and middle indicatives and parse them.
Recognise ten more common verbs.
Recognise second-aorist forms by their changed stem and connect them with their present.
Recognise aorist passive indicatives and parse them.
Recognise perfect and pluperfect indicatives, active and middle-passive, and parse them.
Name the tense of any indicative form of a common verb and connect it with its headword.
Recognise and parse the common forms of δίδωμι, τίθημι, ἵστημι, ἀφίημι and οἶδα.
Recognise the -μι verbs and their commonest compounds.
Parse third-declension nouns with consonant stems and find the stem from the genitive.
Recognise ten common third-declension nouns.
Parse nouns like πόλις, βασιλεύς and γένος and the irregular πατήρ, ἀνήρ, γυνή.
Parse πᾶς, πολύς, μέγας and adjectives in -ης and -ων, and match them to their nouns.
Recognise comparative and superlative forms and read the two ways Greek says 'than'.
Parse the forms of οὗτος and ἐκεῖνος and read them with a noun or alone.
Parse a relative pronoun and find its antecedent: gender and number from the antecedent, case from its own clause.
Tell the interrogative τίς from the indefinite τις and parse either.
Recognise ἑαυτοῦ, ἐμαυτοῦ, σεαυτοῦ and ἀλλήλων, and the declined numerals εἷς, δύο, τρεῖς, τέσσαρες.
Read an adjective or participle with the article as a noun and supply 'man', 'woman', 'thing' or 'people' from its gender and number.
Recognise present and aorist subjunctives by their long vowel and parse them.
Name the commonest uses of the subjunctive in a main clause and after ἐάν, ὅταν and ὃς ἄν.
Recognise a purpose clause with ἵνα or ὅπως and distinguish it from ἵνα giving content or result.
Recognise second- and third-person imperatives, present and aorist, and parse them.
Read the two forms of prohibition: μή with the present imperative and μή with the aorist subjunctive.
Recognise an optative by its οι, αι or ειη and say what it expresses.
Recognise infinitives of every tense and voice and name them.
Parse present and aorist active participles: tense, case, number and gender.
Parse middle and passive participles of every tense.
Say what the choice of present, aorist or perfect stem contributes in an infinitive, participle, subjunctive or imperative.
Classify a conditional sentence by the mood and particle of its 'if' clause and say what it assumes.
Recognise reported speech with ὅτι, with the infinitive and with the participle, and an indirect question.
Read a participle with the article as an adjective clause or as a noun ('the one who…').
Read a participle without the article as a circumstance of the main verb and choose a fitting relation: time, cause, manner, means, condition, concession, purpose.
Recognise a genitive absolute and read it as a clause whose subject is not the subject of the main verb.
Recognise εἰμί with a participle as one verbal expression and name the tense it stands for.
Read an infinitive completing a verb, and an infinitive with the article after a preposition, with its accusative subject.
Mark where a relative or other subordinate clause begins and ends and say what it modifies.
Explain what καί, δέ, γάρ, οὖν, ἀλλά and μέν … δέ signal, and notice a word moved forward for emphasis.
Work through a long sentence in order: find the finite verbs, mark the clauses, attach participles and infinitives, and say what each case is doing.
Read a chapter of John with reduced help and describe what makes John's Greek plain: short clauses, a small vocabulary, καί and asyndeton.
Read 1 John continuously, following its argument through its repeated contrasts.
Read Markan narrative: καὶ εὐθύς, the historical present, the imperfect, and parataxis.
Read Luke's more literary Greek: longer periods, participles, the optative and a larger vocabulary.
Follow a Pauline argument: γάρ and οὖν, rhetorical questions, μὴ γένοιτο, long conditional and causal chains.
Read the imperatival, proverbial Greek of James and the more periodic Greek of 1 Peter.
Read the most literary Greek of the New Testament: balanced periods, rare vocabulary, μέν … δέ.
Read Revelation and notice where its Greek departs from the ordinary rules of agreement.
Read the Didache's Two Ways: imperatives, future used as command, and vocabulary shared with Matthew.
Read 1 Clement's periodic, rhetorical Greek and recognise Septuagint quotation within it.
Read Ignatius's compressed, abrupt style and Polycarp's plainer one, with their new church vocabulary.
Read a chapter of Athanasius: classicising periods, articular infinitives, abstract nouns and the optative.

Give the range of senses of λόγος, φύσις, οὐσία, ὑπόστασις, πρόσωπον, χάρις, πίστις and δικαιοσύνη in the New Testament and in fourth-century use, without reading later definitions back into earlier texts.
